requirement: R5 - signal and staking separated on the leaderboard
separation_rule: The signal table is ranked on evidence strength, never on a return. Its columns are computable with no price at all.
The staking table is empty and stays empty. When a price exists it can demote an entry and can never promote one, so a lucky staking run cannot lift a bad signal.
No column in either table mixes the two: no return, stake or drawdown appears in the signal table, and no forecast accuracy appears in the staking table.

signal_ranking_metric.name: signal score
signal_ranking_metric.why: A bare hit rate rewards a small sample, so the score scales the distance from the reference by the evidence for it. A 60% record on 18 selections cannot outrank a 60% record on 120, and a result consistent with chance scores near zero however large the raw gap looks.

gates.name: Rule pre-registered
gates.rule: The decision rule is written down in code before the results are graded, and no rule is changed after the fact.

gates.name: No look-ahead
gates.rule: A forecast for week w uses only weeks strictly less than w, including the home allowance, the margin spread and the league mean.

gates.name: Minimum settled sample
gates.rule: At least 30 graded selections with a settled official result.

gates.name: Signal survives multiplicity
gates.rule: Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p at most 0.10 across every strategy tested in the same run.

gates.name: Out-of-sample stability
gates.rule: Both halves of the sample beat the reference. Applicable to rate-based strategies only.

gates.name: Executable price captured
gates.rule: The price-snapshot store holds one opening row and one closing row for the market, from a named operator, captured before kickoff.

gates.name: Settlement reproducible
gates.rule: Every graded row re-derives from an official final score, and the whole feed reconciles with the official standings.

gates.name: Leg dependence measured
gates.rule: For a multi-leg strategy, a dependence estimate with a published n exists in correlations.json for exactly that leg structure.

gates.name: No parameter fitted in the window
gates.rule: Every parameter is either a published constant or measured from weeks before the game being forecast. Nothing is fitted on the evaluation window.

gates.name: Source rights cleared
gates.rule: Written permission exists to retain and release the source material behind any published price. Not evidenced for NFL.com.
gates.blocks: Live tier, and release of any dataset.

gate_rule: A gate marked n/a leaves the denominator and is never counted as a pass.

tiers.Paper: Default. Rules and settlement are sound; the signal has not cleared the evidence bar.
tiers.Provisional: G03, G04, G05 and G08 clear. Published for review; no reward, no stake.
tiers.Live: Provisional plus G06 (executable price) and G10 (source rights). Only a live strategy is exposed to the demotion gate.
tiers.Blocked on data: The official numbers needed to grade the strategy were never retrieved, so the performance gates do not apply.
tiers.Control: Published to demonstrate a property of the test - a forecast graded against its own number, or a slip whose legs are the same event. A control is never ranked and never promoted.

rewards.prize_eligibility: A reward requires the live tier, which requires G06. The price store holds zero rows, so no entry is eligible.
rewards.what_is_being_ranked: Signal only. Ranking never uses a stake, a return or a bankroll, because none of those exist here.

staking_table.empty_because: No consulted official source publishes an executable price, so there is no stake, no return, no drawdown and no closing-line value. Blank by rule.
staking_table.effect_on_signal_rank: None. Ever. By construction: the signal rank is computed before the staking table is read.
